messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-IR-2026 - high GPU memory pressure on dedicated-pool-west2a. affected_nodes=3, candidate_evacuations=2. Automated fallback enabled to model variant 'small-quant-v1'. Auto-suppress in 3m if acked.

pagerduty: Incident PD-IR-2026 triggered by rule: gpu.memory_pressure > 85% for 2m. Escalation: oncall -> alex.

alex: acked. looking at metrics now. live grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/p/dedicated-gpu-west2a

maria: noted. any customer-facing errors? seeing a small bump in 500s from dedicated endpoints. p50 latency up ~120ms. :eyes:

alex: logs show repeated cuda errors on pod dedicated-infer-47: 
```
[2025-11-07T02:03:11Z] ERROR runtime: CUDA_ALLOC_RETRY: failed to allocate 1.2G on GPU0
[2025-11-07T02:03:11Z] WARN kvcache: eviction spike +120%
[2025-11-07T02:03:12Z] INFO fallback: routing to small-quant-v1 for session a3f2
```

alex: running quick probe: kubectl -n infer logs -l pool=dedicated-west2a --since=10m | grep -E "CUDA_ALLOC|OOM|kvcache"

sre-bot: Suggestion: mute non-critical alert rules on this pool for 10m to reduce noise. To apply run: `/sre mute gpu.memory_pressure dedicated-pool-west2a 10m`

maria: /sre mute applied. also creating a short customer note that some ded customers may see degraded throughput but no data loss. tagging @customer-success.

alex: temporary mitigation: 1) scaling up pool by +2 GPUs via autoscale-burst 2) drain the two busiest pods for graceful restart 3) confirm fallback routing is stable. Kicking commands now.

sam: observed one customer job in particular (cust-842) kept pinned to large model variant; opened quick patch to allow fallback routing. patch: `allow-fallback=true` deployed to router.

alex: drain started on pod dedicated-infer-47: `kubectl drain dedicated-infer-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` - waiting for replacement pod.

kai: stepping in for oncall rotation in ~10m. any blockers for handoff?

alex: no blockers. summary: PD-IR-2026 GPU mem pressure on dedicated-pool-west2a caused by kvcache eviction storm + one noisy customer job that pinned large-model allocations. Automated small-model fallback triggered and reduced 5xxs. Actions taken: muted noisy alerts, autoscale +2 GPUs, drained noisy pods, router patch to allow fallback for pinned jobs. Estimated customer impact: some increased latency, small burst of 500s for ~4m. Next steps for next oncall: watch for repeated CUDA_ALLOC failures, monitor kvcache eviction rate and consider kv cache size cap.

kai: ack. taking over at 02:16 UTC. will monitor for 30m and keep PD updated. thanks. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PD-IR-2026: ack updated - handoff to kai. incident status: mitigation in progress.

alex: marking runbook note: `gpu-oom-fasthand` steps executed, adding logs and command history to incident doc.

sre-bot: tip: consider adding a preemptive route that limits large-model session concurrency per-customer to 2 in this pool. filing follow-up ticket.

kai: resolved? not yet. will close when kvcache eviction < 10/min for 10m and CUDA errors stop. will update thread.

incident-bot: PD-IR-2026: update - autoscale succeeded, new pods provisioned, fallback remained active for pinned sessions. Monitoring thresholds improving.

kai: 02:22 UTC - CUDA errors dropped to zero, eviction rate ~4/min. marking as resolved in 15m if stable.

incident-bot: PD-IR-2026 resolved at 1757771360. auto-close can be overridden by pager duty.

maria: thanks all — adding postmortem notes and customer comm draft.

sam: adding the noisy job id to blacklist for this pool for 24h to prevent re-pin.
__notes: generated thread about automated paging and live mitigation for GPU memory pressure; uses realistic Slack style, includes bot notices, commands, code block logs.
